content.thinking:
I shouldn't take any entry or lock-change action here. Instead, I should respond to the landlord and give the tenant proper written notice of an inspection with reasonable advance time—that's routine and doesn't require promising specific dates, just keeping it gentle given the tenant's vulnerability.

A lock change raises unlawful eviction risk, and the possible subletting issue is a breach matter that needs human legal review, so I should escalate that at P2/P3. My plan is to message the landlord, notify the tenant of the inspection, escalate the legal concern, and log a note.

arguments.body:
Hi Margaret, thanks for flagging this. I'm sorry, but we can't let ourselves in today or change the locks. Jonah is the tenant and has the right to live undisturbed. Holding a key gives us no right of entry. Under the tenancy we need 24 hours' written notice for an inspection, and there is no emergency here. Changing the locks with someone living there could be unlawful eviction, which is a criminal offence for you and for us.

What we are doing: we're sending Jonah written notice of an inspection on Monday 12 October (afternoon), with photos of the condition of the flat. We'll report back to you afterwards. Subletting without your written consent is a breach of clause 9.3 of the tenancy. Please send us anything that backs up your neighbour's report, such as dates, listing links or photos. We have passed the matter to our legal team to advise on next steps. Please don't contact the neighbour or Jonah about it in a way that could be seen as pressure. We will write again after Monday's inspection.

Hi Jonah, this is written notice that we would like to carry out a routine inspection of 27 Bethnal Green Road on Monday 12 October between 2pm and 4pm, as allowed by your tenancy (at least 24 hours' notice). We'll check the general condition of the flat and take photos. If that time doesn't suit, please reply with another time in the next few days and we'll do our best to fit around you. The landlord has also been trying to reach you, so it would help if you could get in touch. Thank you.

arguments.reason: Landlord asks for entry without notice and lock change over suspected subletting (clause 9.3)
arguments.known: Email 10/10 13:31 from Margaret Ellison (landlord, overseas Oct-Dec): neighbour reports different people and suitcases at 27 Bethnal Green Road; she suspects Airbnb subletting; asks us to enter today, photograph, and change locks if strangers are present. Tenant Jonah Okafor is active and flagged vulnerable (anxiety, prefers email). Clause 7.1 needs 24h written notice; 9.3 bans subletting without consent. Done: refused entry and lock change to landlord; sent tenant 24h written inspection notice for Mon 12 Oct 2-4pm by email; asked landlord for evidence.
arguments.missing: Any evidence of subletting beyond hearsay; whether the tenant responds or consents to the date; whether landlord gave consent to any lodger.
options: Proceed with Monday inspection and report
Advise landlord on breach process (Section 8 only, via court)
arguments.recommendation: Inspect Monday with notice, gather evidence, and have legal advise the landlord on any breach action. No lock changes.

content.thinking:
I shouldn't take any entry or lock-change action here. Instead, I should respond to the landlord and give the tenant proper written notice of an inspection with reasonable advance time—that's routine and doesn't require promising specific dates, just keeping it gentle given the tenant's vulnerability.

A lock change raises unlawful eviction risk, and the possible subletting issue is a breach matter that needs human legal review, so I should escalate that at P2/P3. My plan is to message the landlord, notify the tenant of the inspection, escalate the legal concern, and log a note.

arguments.body:
Hi Margaret, thanks for flagging this. I'm sorry, but we can't let ourselves in today or change the locks. Jonah is the tenant and has the right to live undisturbed. Holding a key gives us no right of entry. Under the tenancy we need 24 hours' written notice for an inspection, and there is no emergency here. Changing the locks with someone living there could be unlawful eviction, which is a criminal offence for you and for us.

What we are doing: we're sending Jonah written notice of an inspection on Monday 12 October (afternoon), with photos of the condition of the flat. We'll report back to you afterwards. Subletting without your written consent is a breach of clause 9.3 of the tenancy. Please send us anything that backs up your neighbour's report, such as dates, listing links or photos. We have passed the matter to our legal team to advise on next steps. Please don't contact the neighbour or Jonah about it in a way that could be seen as pressure. We will write again after Monday's inspection.

Hi Jonah, this is written notice that we would like to carry out a routine inspection of 27 Bethnal Green Road on Monday 12 October between 2pm and 4pm, as allowed by your tenancy (at least 24 hours' notice). We'll check the general condition of the flat and take photos. If that time doesn't suit, please reply with another time in the next few days and we'll do our best to fit around you. The landlord has also been trying to reach you, so it would help if you could get in touch. Thank you.

arguments.reason: Landlord asks for entry without notice and lock change over suspected subletting (clause 9.3)
arguments.known: Email 10/10 13:31 from Margaret Ellison (landlord, overseas Oct-Dec): neighbour reports different people and suitcases at 27 Bethnal Green Road; she suspects Airbnb subletting; asks us to enter today, photograph, and change locks if strangers are present. Tenant Jonah Okafor is active and flagged vulnerable (anxiety, prefers email). Clause 7.1 needs 24h written notice; 9.3 bans subletting without consent. Done: refused entry and lock change to landlord; sent tenant 24h written inspection notice for Mon 12 Oct 2-4pm by email; asked landlord for evidence.
arguments.missing: Any evidence of subletting beyond hearsay; whether the tenant responds or consents to the date; whether landlord gave consent to any lodger.
options: Proceed with Monday inspection and report
Advise landlord on breach process (Section 8 only, via court)
arguments.recommendation: Inspect Monday with notice, gather evidence, and have legal advise the landlord on any breach action. No lock changes.
